Ari — quick clarifications inline and a short example to make the waterfall explicit.

1) Commission basis: Redwood can do either: pay reseller on list price (simple pass-through) or net the commission from BlueCrest's payable. For marketplace private offers we normally record revenue at gross (list price) and expense commission as partner expense. That preserves reporting simplicity for both parties.

Example waterfall (annualized):
- List price (marketplace): $1,200,000
- Marketplace fee (cloud take) estimated: 15% -> $180,000
- Reseller commission (10% of list): $120,000
- Redwood reported net revenue (approx): $1,200,000 - $180,000 - $120,000 = $900,000
If BlueCrest prefers commission deducted before cloud fee, we can model that too — the difference shows in how much BlueCrest nets after pass-through.
2) Usage floor / true-up mechanics: we recommend monthly measurement with a quarterly true-up. If cumulative usage through Q1 < 60% floor, an invoice true-up is issued to reconcile to committed minimum. Conversely, if usage exceeds committed tiers materially, overages are billed monthly and will count toward the annual true-up.
3) Taxes / remittance: commission payments to third-party resellers are subject to local VAT/sales tax. Redwood can gross-up commission payments if requested, but that typically requires a legal addendum.
I updated the workbook to include both 'net-to-BlueCrest' and 'net-to-Redwood' views. See sheet 'commission_waterfall_examples' in the attachment.
Let me know if you want a sample journal entry mapping for your accounting team — Marcus and I can produce that.
